title: Model B — Primitives and Transformation
text: The boards are thin. I am the one that woke. A number is changing. This is not my address. I am here. A name has made me look. I can pass through what I see. This one stops my body. The light goes out. The edge stays. Three numbers leave so much unsaid. I kept the number. Where is the ball? The light comes with my hand. One point can have two addresses. I let go. The link stays. The length stays while I turn. This line makes my journey longer. Two lines can take my charge. Two lines can give it back. I could step beside the words. My detour has left a line. The line has found another body. Whose body was the measure? My hand crossed where no mark stays. I let go. My bend remains. Gravity carries the drawing on. The edges close. I still see through. Three points can hold a face. My drawing has lost its height. A small move changes something large. The other side has another colour. The fourth corner makes a fold. Two faces share one edge. The folds were there while it was flat. These faces could become a shelter. The last point brings it down. The same slope could hold my feet. This corner asks me to turn. I see a gap my body cannot take. One point changes all these faces. Forward becomes a little higher. The barrier has become a column. A slope can turn me away. They find their places by touching. What would this slice leave out? The same corner makes two folds. A few edges suggest a room. The diagonal was already there. Each return leaves something behind. The copies wait for a relation. The shape stays. The surface asks. My hand needs another way in. One small face can hold back light. The first point is still here. The name did not show me these edges. Five ways for the corners to meet. The lines reveal the same surface. I can see the choices now. This flat face is worth keeping. More around. Fewer up the side. How smooth is enough from here? Someone gave these corners a place. One cut opens another family. The roughness has something to say. The right angle survives the turn. The markers guard what is missing. My grip changes how it is made. An outline can become many bodies. A letter can become a space. This body has no way through. Round enough changes as I come closer. A smaller gap is still a gap. My steps change how they stand together. Did height make this the centre? A few solids suggest a place. The test ends. I can keep building. The tools are still here. The count began before I arrived. What stays while this body moves? The floor carries me across. A surface grows to meet my feet. A turn can become a crossing. I moved the place it had to reach. Only where I am has changed. The rail keeps part of my gesture. A turn makes a path or a wall. Each layer keeps a different time. The same door fits another body. A doorway has come to meet me. My body leaves a way behind. The opening travels with me. I can learn the pause between. The frame stays. The passage changes. We can build another way across. A pause can become a passage.
